note: The main banks: the three largest US banks by consolidated assets in the Federal Reserve's list of large commercial banks are JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citibank. Chase's full personal range is written; Bank of America's and Citi's are not, and neither is Capital One's, tried in their place. Bank of America's terms and conditions page loads each card's disclosure from secure.bankofamerica.com, which answered with a captcha (not circumvented); Citi's and Capital One's card pages load their pricing by script from their application systems (Citi's page didn't finish loading when rendered), so no card's terms could be read from them on 2026-10-30. Chase: every personal card on its all-credit-cards page (read 2026-10-30), 32 of them, each from its own Pricing and Terms page (the costs accurate as of 9/22/2026, the Prime Rate 7.00% that day); the 11 business cards (Ink, Sapphire Reserve for Business, the United, Southwest, IHG and Hyatt business cards) aren't written. Each card's purchase APR is written as its range, the bank setting each holder's rate within it by creditworthiness; a 0% introductory purchase APR for its months where the card has one; the annual membership fee (the United Explorer's $0 first year written as its first year waived; the Sapphire Reserve's $195 for each authorized user isn't written); the cash advance APR and fee (the greater of a floor and a share of the advance); the foreign transaction fee (written as 0 where the box says None); the late payment and returned payment fees, each 'up to' a figure, written at that figure; and the penalty APR, 'up to' a figure, written at it. The due date is at least 21 days after each billing cycle closes and no interest is charged on purchases if the whole balance is paid by then; that is the least time the bank promises, not the most a purchase goes without interest, so no grace is written. Balance transfer APRs and fees, the Chase Pay Over Time fee (a plan the holder chooses) and the Military Lending Act terms aren't written; the boxes state no over-limit fee (None), no minimum payment and no limit rule. The Amazon and Prime Visa cards' late and returned payment fees are up to $39 and their cash advance fee the greater of $5 or 4%. The earlier reading of the Freedom Unlimited (2026-10-29) is kept as a source; its figures hold.
